root_idea.summary: The root centers on leaving, releasing, or withdrawing from something, whether by choice or under compulsion.
root_idea.development: From this core develop the notions of abandonment, what is left behind as a remainder or inheritance, and things left solitary or unused. A special transitive construction means causing something to remain in a state, while derived reciprocal forms express mutual relinquishment or truce.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Independent Quran-attested Form I verb with several lexically supported Quranic constructions.

senses.definition: To leave, forsake, relinquish, abandon, desert, or quit someone, something, or a place.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic use covers departure, abandonment, and leaving something alone or untouched; it may occur intentionally or under compulsion. Active, imperative, and passive forms express the corresponding grammatical relations.

senses.definition: To leave something behind as a remainder, possession, or inheritance.
senses.usage_conditions: Used especially of what remains after a person’s death or departure, including property or people left behind.

senses.definition: To make or cause someone or something to be in a specified state.
senses.usage_conditions: A doubly transitive construction in which the object is caused to remain or become in the state expressed by the complement, as in being left in darkness.

senses.definition: To leave a lasting remembrance, praise, or legacy for someone among later generations.
senses.usage_conditions: Especially the construction وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرِينَ, in which what is left is a lasting good mention or eulogy.

senses.definition: One who leaves, forsakes, relinquishes, or abandons.
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle may describe a person who gives something up or leaves someone or something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cease, desist, refrain from, neglect, omit, or leave an act undone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical extension used with an action, duty, right, or other matter as the object; it includes leaving a right unclaimed or a prayer unit unperformed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave nothing undone; to exert oneself fully.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII usage in the expression فَمَا اتَّرَكَ, meaning that nothing within one’s power was omitted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To marry, taking as wife a تَرِيكَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The تَرِيكَة is explicitly described as a woman who has remained unmarried and virgin until middle age or long after puberty in her parents’ home.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mutually relinquish or leave one another unmolested; by extension, to make peace or a truce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III reciprocal or concurrent construction, including leaving an affair or commodity between the parties in its existing state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiomatic expression, to preserve or prolong someone’s life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributed idiomatic use in which تَارَكَ is equated with أَبْقَى, ‘to preserve’ or ‘keep alive.’
A Form VI reciprocal construction referring to parties jointly giving up or leaving an affair between them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A drinking cup or bowl carried or lifted with both hands.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: As a collective noun it denotes the nation; تُرْكِيٌّ is the singular nisba and may also mean Turkish.
An explicitly marked figurative or assumed-tropical usage; a plural تَرَكَاتٌ is reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a traditional expression, Hagar and Ishmael as what was left behind; the expression is explained metaphorically through an ostrich egg abandoned by its mother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic or metaphorical usage associated with a traditional report, not a general ordinary meaning of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing left, forsaken, or abandoned; especially the property or inheritance left by a deceased person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes what a person leaves behind and, in particular, the estate inherited after death.
Used as an emphatic imperative, including the repeated expression تَرَاكِ تَرَاكِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman left unmarried who has remained a virgin until middle age or long after puberty in her parents’ home.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source explicitly restricts this lexical item to a woman, not a male; its plural is تَرَائِكُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A meadow or pasture left neglected, or reduced to remnants after grazing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote land whose depasturing has been neglected or whose vegetation has largely been consumed.
A specialized usage for residual water after the passage of a torrent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An egg left after the young bird has emerged, especially an ostrich egg forsaken in the desert.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to an empty egg or to an ostrich egg left solitary by the female.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron helmet, by analogy with an abandoned egg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An explicitly marked figurative extension based on the egg sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A date raceme left bare after its dates or other contents have been shaken off or eaten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural usage for a raceme from which what was upon it has disappeared.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perpetuated conditions of hope and heedlessness in people that embolden them toward worldly pursuits.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributed traditional and figurative usage describing conditions maintained among mankind.
